title: Select K Disjoint Special Substrings
summary: Given a string s and an integer k, decide if it's feasible to choose k non-overlapping special substrings.
statement: Given a string s and an integer k, decide if it's feasible to choose k non-overlapping special substrings. A special substring is one where each character within it does not appear elsewhere in the string, and the substring is not the whole string s.
constraints: A special substring is not all of s and every character it contains occurs nowhere outside it.
Return whether at least k pairwise non-overlapping special substrings can be selected.
hints: A special substring is a closed interval containing every global occurrence of each character it touches.
Construct the minimal valid closure from each character’s first occurrence, then greedily schedule valid intervals by end.
Expand the right edge using last occurrences; reject if any character began before the start; exclude the whole string and count disjoint intervals.
Minimal closures dominate larger choices, and earliest-finish interval scheduling maximizes how many non-overlapping closures fit.
editorial: Minimal closures dominate larger choices, and earliest-finish interval scheduling maximizes how many non-overlapping closures fit.

tests.explanation: Two closed character intervals can be selected without overlap.
The only closed interval is the whole string, which is forbidden, so return false.
